# Countermodel and hostile-case ledger

| Candidate statement | Hostile case | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| The conditional minimizer is a unique group element. | `SU(2)`, endpoint `-I` lies at the cut locus. | Counterexample. The minimizing set is a conjugacy sphere. The manuscript uses fixed distances on the entire set. |
| Pointwise heat-kernel asymptotics are enough for setwise probabilities. | Good sets approach endpoints and the cut locus. | Rejected proof route. Uniform Varadhan asymptotics and a compact Laplace lemma are used. |
| The exact center boundary is harmless because it has Haar measure zero. | Perturb every staple slightly. | Counterexample to the dismissal. A uniform energy gap persists on an open positive-measure neighborhood. |
| One adverse boundary pair can violate the Dobrushin row criterion. | A single coefficient can approach one from below while the row remains below one. | Insufficient. The proof constructs `m` distinct opposite-link coefficients, each tending to one. |
| The theorem covers every compact simple group. | Trivial-center groups such as the adjoint form `SO(3)`. | False universal quantifier. The theorem explicitly assumes a nonidentity center. |
| The threshold case has bad probability tending to one. | `rho=b_*`, where the minimizing set is on the event boundary. | Not established. Only zero exponential rate is asserted. |
| The one-frustrated displacement persists for `k` frustrated staples. | `k=0,m` and `k=m/2`. | False. The displacement is `kL/m`; Proposition 5.1 records all cases. |
| Dobrushin failure proves nonuniqueness. | Sufficient criteria need not be necessary. | Rejected inference; not claimed. |
| Local central frustration is a global twisted sector. | Open block has no periodic flux class. | Rejected identification; literature comparison separates the objects. |
